host_applicability: node; bun (unproven); deno; browser-wasm rejects write with 'The \"write\" option is unavailable in this environment'
operation_specific_holes: esbuild writes into a caller-selected destination it does not stage or atomically publish; 0.28.2's changelog states input files are protected from overwrite without --allow-overwrite by not writing any files when a build error is encountered, and that this protection had regressed since 0.17.0 - so the protection is a 0.28.2+ fact only. Nothing upstream states what happens on interruption mid-write.
cancellation_and_interruption: No provider cancellation. Interruption releases the fiber while the native child may still be writing. Publication is provider-direct-durable: no staging, no atomic rename, no rollback, and partial durable output after failure or interruption must be declared possible.
diagnostics_ownership: Same as ESB-OP-01. A failed build additionally produces a BuildFailure Error carrying errors and warnings arrays.
recommendation_rationale: Native, default, and unavoidable for consumers who want esbuild's own output topology (chunks, assets, maps, css bundles). It ships only with an explicit provider-direct-durable publication law and an explicit no-rollback statement, per the reconciliation's lifecycle-specific publication rule.
gate_before_freeze: P-ESB-13 partial-write and remnant enumeration under induced failure; P-ESB-14 interruption during write; P-ESB-15 allowOverwrite and pre-existing destination behavior at 0.28.2 versus <=0.28.1

operation_specific_holes: Plugins are refused with 'Cannot use plugins in synchronous API calls'. The call does not use the shared long-lived child: it either delegates to a worker_thread (default) or runs execFileSync with maxBuffer = ESBUILD_MAX_BUFFER || 16 MiB, so sufficiently large output fails with ENOBUFS. Throws on deno ('does not work in Deno') and browser ('only works in node').
cancellation_and_interruption: None. The call blocks the calling thread to completion. There is no interruption point at all: an Effect wrapping it cannot be interrupted and must not claim to be.
diagnostics_ownership: Same inherited-stderr caveat; the worker-thread path additionally reconstructs synthetic build errors (fakeBuildError) rather than forwarding native ones.
recommendation_rationale: A blocking, non-interruptible call contradicts AGENTS.md's interruption law (interruption closes Scope and terminates active children) and Effect's fiber model; wrapping it would be a false interruption promise. It also loses plugin authority, imposes an undocumented 16 MiB output ceiling, and does not exist on two of four hosts. ESB-OP-01 is the complete migration target.
gate_before_freeze: none - rejection is decided on the declarations and shipped implementation and needs no probe

sub_operations: context.rebuild (ESB-SUB-01); context.watch (ESB-SUB-02); context.serve (ESB-SUB-03); context.cancel (ESB-SUB-04); context.dispose (ESB-SUB-05); plugin build.resolve (ESB-SUB-06); plugin onStart/onEnd/onResolve/onLoad/onDispose (ESB-SUB-07..11); serve onRequest (ESB-SUB-12)
request_modes_and_modifiers: every ESB-OP-01 mode, captured once at acquisition and immutable thereafter; WatchOptions.delay; the full ServeOptions record
result_fields: rebuild returns the same BuildResult shape as ESB-OP-01; serve returns ServeResult {port, hosts}; watch, cancel and dispose return void
host_applicability: node; bun (unproven); deno; browser-wasm can create a context but its watch and serve both throw 'Cannot use the \watch\" API in this environment' / '... \"serve\" ...'"
operation_specific_holes: Options are captured at acquisition and cannot be changed per rebuild. rebuild() coalesces: concurrent calls share one latestResultPromise, so N calls yield one result value, not N builds. Watch-triggered rebuild results are delivered only through a plugin onEnd callback - there is no watch result channel and WatchOptions carries nothing but delay. serve() returns no stop handle; the server dies only with dispose(). rebuild/watch/serve are not guarded by the didDispose flag, so their post-dispose behavior is decided by the native child, not by a typed JS error.
cancellation_and_interruption: cancel() is best-effort: it resolves on any response, never rejects, and silently resolves after dispose. dispose() is idempotent, but it resolves before plugin onDispose callbacks run - those are scheduled with setTimeout(cb, 0) after the promise settles. A live context holds a ref on the shared child, so a leaked context keeps the host event loop alive.
diagnostics_ownership: esbuild owns all diagnostics. The inherited-stderr caveat applies. If a build response carries writeToStdout, the JS layer prints it with console.log to the host stdout.
recommendation_rationale: D7 explicitly authorises exposing esbuild context watch and serve as native operations in 0.4, and the recorded execution at 0.28.1/0.28.2 exercised context -> rebuild -> rebuild -> cancel -> dispose. It is the one operation in the whole corpus that genuinely earns a scoped handle: it owns a real provider lifetime, and Scope closure maps onto dispose(). rebuild/watch/serve/cancel/dispose stay methods of this one state owner - no evidence at 0.28.2 establishes an independently acquirable or independently releasable sub-resource.
gate_before_freeze: P-ESB-01 rebuild/cancel/dispose race matrix; P-ESB-02 post-dispose rebuild/watch/serve; P-ESB-03 dispose during active watch and during active serve; P-ESB-04 rebuild coalescing under concurrency; P-ESB-05 plugin onDispose completion versus dispose() settlement; P-ESB-06 context leak and host event-loop liveness

request_type: BuildOptions with write:true and outfile or outdir
request_modes_and_modifiers: every ESB-OP-02 mode, captured once at acquisition; WatchOptions.delay; the full ServeOptions record
operation_specific_holes: All of ESB-OP-11's holes, plus: every rebuild and every watch-triggered rebuild republishes into the same caller-selected destination with no staging and no rollback, so a watch session produces an unbounded sequence of provider-direct-durable mutations. Interruption at any point can leave a mixed-generation output tree.
recommendation_rationale: Split from ESB-OP-11 because its failure and publication laws differ, exactly as RECONCILIATION section 1 requires. It is the mode a watch or serve session actually needs, so refusing it would make context watch useless.
gate_before_freeze: all ESB-OP-11 probes, plus P-ESB-07 remnants after interrupting a watch-triggered rebuild mid-write; P-ESB-08 output tree generation coherence during an active watch

host_applicability: node (returns Promise.resolve() immediately, without awaiting child exit); deno (async, awaits stopService); browser
operation_specific_holes: Absent entirely from the imported inventory rows E01-E12. It is process-global, not per-context: one module-global longLivedService is shared by every one-shot build, every transform, and every live context in the host process, including contexts created by unrelated libraries. Calling it destroys stdin/stdout and sends child.kill() (default SIGTERM), then clears longLivedService - so the very next API call transparently respawns a new child. It is a reset, not a terminal release. On node it resolves before any exit is observed.
cancellation_and_interruption: Not a cancellation mechanism. It cannot be scoped to one operation.
recommendation_rationale: Exposing this - or worse, calling it from a Scope finalizer - would let one effect-build scope terminate the native engine underneath every other live esbuild context in the process, including contexts effect-build does not own. That violates the shared-lifecycle ownership laws and creates cross-owner interference that no type can express. It must remain uncalled and unexposed; esbuild's own unref() already keeps the child from blocking host exit on node.
gate_before_freeze: P-ESB-09 confirm the unref'd child does not block process exit on the bun host, where child_process semantics are not proven

request_modes_and_modifiers: wasmURL, wasmModule and worker are all rejected on node and deno with 'only works in the browser'
host_applicability: browser (mandatory precondition before any other call); node and deno (accepts only an empty options object; its whole effect is to eagerly spawn the shared child)
operation_specific_holes: Absent entirely from the imported inventory rows E01-E12. It sets a module-global initializeWasCalled latch and throws 'Cannot call \initialize\" more than once' on the second call. stop() resets the latch on node."
recommendation_rationale: On the hosts effect-build targets it does nothing a first API call would not do, and it consumes a one-shot process-global latch: if effect-build calls it, a consumer's own later initialize() throws. A library must not spend a global once-only token on its user's behalf.

request_type: argv, cwd, env, and stdin bytes for the explicitly selected esbuild executable
result_type: exit status, collected stdout bytes, stderr bytes
request_modes_and_modifiers: every CLI flag from the binary's own --help; input arrives on stdin or as an entry-point argument; no outfile or outdir; --loader for the stdin unit; --analyze and --analyze=verbose add a report to stdout; --log-style; --color
result_fields: bundled output bytes on stdout, human diagnostics on stderr, process exit status
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process; the selected binary is a per-platform native executable (or a node-run WebAssembly module on the three fallback platforms)
operation_specific_holes: No plugins, no callbacks, no rebuild handle, and no structured result object - the compatibility matrix already records the CLI/context pairing as a lane mismatch rather than a version failure. The candidate must collect finite stdout before returning; a raw stream would be a separate scoped-process identity.
cancellation_and_interruption: Effect Scope owns the child. Termination is a signal to the selected process; the reaping and descendant laws are the shared lifecycle code's, not esbuild's.
diagnostics_ownership: The CLI emits human-formatted diagnostics on stderr. They are bytes, not a Message[]; effect-build must not parse them into structured diagnostics.
recommendation_rationale: Selected-binary and process authority is a real semantic distinction that D2 and D5 both preserve, and this lane is the only one that lets a consumer pin an exact executable rather than an npm resolution. It ships with a mandatory preflight that records which of the two possible bin forms was selected (see REL-ESB-03).
gate_before_freeze: P-ESB-21 bounded stdout/stderr collection with independent limits and truncation facts; P-ESB-22 signal delivery and exit observation through both bin forms; P-ESB-23 stdin-fed build with --loader

request_modes_and_modifiers: --outfile; --outdir; --outbase; --allow-overwrite; --entry-names/--chunk-names/--asset-names; --out-extension; --public-path; --metafile=PATH (writes a JSON file - unlike the API's metafile result field); --mangle-cache=PATH (writes a JSON file); plus every ESB-OP-15 flag

cancellation_and_interruption: Effect Scope owns the child; a terminated build may leave partial durable output exactly as in ESB-OP-02, with no staging and no rollback.
recommendation_rationale: Same rationale as ESB-OP-15; split from it because its publication law is provider-direct-durable rather than none.
gate_before_freeze: ESB-OP-15's probes plus P-ESB-24 remnants after signalling a direct-write CLI build mid-run; P-ESB-25 --metafile and --mangle-cache file publication and overwrite behavior

request_type: argv including --watch, cwd, env, and an open stdin
result_type: a scoped child-process handle plus raw byte streams
result_fields: interleaved human rebuild reports on stderr, repeated durable writes, and eventual process exit
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process
operation_specific_holes: This is not a semantic twin of ESB-SUB-02 (context.watch): there is no callback channel, no BuildResult, no delay-only options record, and no shared engine - it is a separate process whose only machine-observable facts are bytes, exit status, and files on disk. At argv level --watch is a modifier on an ordinary build invocation, not a subcommand, so it composes with --serve. Its lifetime is additionally bound to stdin: the binary's own --help states watch 'stops when stdin is closed, use \--watch=forever\" to ignore stdin'."
cancellation_and_interruption: Two independent termination channels exist - closing stdin and signalling the process - and they are not equivalent. Scope closure must choose and document one. D7 forbids any typed Ready/Rebuilt protocol here.
diagnostics_ownership: Human text only. REC-006 remains falsified: no typed event may be derived from these bytes.
recommendation_rationale: D7 authorises raw scoped command watch as a process handle with byte streams in 0.4 and explicitly says raw scoped command handles do not wait for the typed-protocol research. The stdin-close termination channel is new evidence that makes this operation more, not less, worth exposing honestly.
gate_before_freeze: P-ESB-26 stdin-close versus signal termination, including through the node-shim bin form; P-ESB-27 descendant reaping when the selected bin is a node shim; P-ESB-28 durable output state after abrupt termination mid-rebuild

result_type: a scoped child-process handle plus raw byte streams; the bound address is printed as human text
result_fields: HTTP responses to clients; the bound host and port appear only in human stdout/stderr text
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process
operation_specific_holes: Not a semantic twin of ESB-SUB-03 (context.serve): the in-process serve returns a structured ServeResult {port, hosts} and supports an onRequest callback and a structured cors object; the CLI has neither. It is also a flag on an ordinary build invocation rather than a subcommand.
cancellation_and_interruption: Scope closure signals the process. The listening socket's release is not separately observable.
recommendation_rationale: A serve operation whose caller cannot learn the bound port is close to useless, and at 0.28.2 the CLI reports the address only as human text - which REC-006 and D7 forbid parsing. That leaves the operation honest only when the caller pins an exact port, which is a narrow enough case that it should wait for a demonstrated consumer. GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr also shows the served directory is a real attack surface with a host-specific hole, and no probe evidence exists for any serve behavior at any coordinate.
gate_before_freeze: unblocked only by (a) an upstream machine-readable address channel, or (b) an explicit product decision that the operation requires a pinned port; then P-ESB-29 port binding and release, P-ESB-30 termination with in-flight requests

request_type: BuildOptions with write:true and neither outfile nor outdir
result_type: Promise<BuildResult> whose outputFiles is absent; the bundled bytes are not in the result
result_fields: errors and warnings only - the actual output is written to the host process stdout
operation_specific_holes: Absent entirely from the imported inventory rows E01-E12 and from the imported crosswalk. When the native child returns a writeToStdout payload, the JavaScript layer prints it to the host process stdout with console.log and strips one trailing newline. The bytes are therefore neither a returned value nor a file: they are an uncapturable side effect on a stream the library does not own.
cancellation_and_interruption: No provider cancellation; the side effect may already have occurred when the fiber is interrupted.
diagnostics_ownership: The output itself, not just diagnostics, escapes onto the host's stdout.
recommendation_rationale: A library must never write a consumer's build output to the consumer's stdout. This mode has no result value to return and no publication effect-build can observe, own, or clean up. effect-build's request validation must make it unreachable by requiring write:false or a destination, and must say so as a typed preflight refusal rather than silently rewriting the caller's options.
gate_before_freeze: P-ESB-10 confirm the exact BuildOptions combinations that reach the writeToStdout path, so preflight refuses precisely that set and nothing more
